Two blocks of masses, \(1~\text{kg}\) and \(2~\text{kg},\) are placed one above the other on a smooth horizontal table. The coefficient of static friction between the blocks is \(0.5.\) A horizontal force \(F\) is applied to the \(2~\text{kg}\) block. What is the maximum value of \(F\) for which the two blocks move together without slipping? questions.question:
A body of mass \(m\) is projected upward along a rough inclined plane that makes an angle of \(30^{\circ}\) with the horizontal. It is observed that the time of ascent is exactly half the time of descent. What is the coefficient of friction between the body and the incline?
1.\(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{5}\)2.\(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{5}\)
3.\(\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\)4.\(\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(t=\sqrt{\dfrac{2S}{a}} \) Step 1: Find the acceleration of body during ascent. \(mg\sin\theta+f=ma\) \(\Rightarrow mg\sin\theta+\mu mg\cos\theta=ma\) \(\Rightarrow a=g\sin\theta+\mu g\cos\theta\) Step 2: Find the acceleration of body during decent. \(mg\sin\theta-f=ma'\) \(\Rightarrow mg\sin\theta-\mu mg\cos\theta=ma'\) \(\Rightarrow a'=g\sin\theta-\mu g\cos\theta\) Step 3:Find the coefficient of friction between the body and the plane. \(t_a=\dfrac{1}{2}t_d \) \(\Rightarrow \sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{a}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{2s}{a'}} \) \(\Rightarrow a=4a' \) \(\Rightarrow g\sin\theta+\mu g\cos\theta=4(g\sin\theta-\mu g\cos\theta) \) \(\Rightarrow \tan\theta+\mu=4(\tan\theta-\mu) \) \(\Rightarrow \tan30^{\circ}+\mu=4(\tan30^{\circ}-\mu) \) \(\Rightarrow \mu=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{5} \) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
A racing car of mass \(m\) is moving at a constant speed \(v\) along a flat, horizontal circular track of radius \(R.\) The coefficient of static friction between the tyres and the track is \(\mu_s.\) In addition to its weight, the car experiences a downward aerodynamic force (negative lift) of magnitude \(F_L.\) Assume that the static friction is at its limiting value and that the frictional forces on all four tyres are identical. The magnitude of \(F_L\) is:
1.\(m\left(\dfrac{v^2}{\mu_s R}-g\right) \)2.\(-m\left(g+\dfrac{v^2}{\mu_s R}\right)\)
3.\(m\left(g-\dfrac{v^2}{\mu_s R}\right)\)4.\(m\left(\dfrac{v^2}{\mu_s R}+g\right)\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(f_s=\dfrac{mv^2}{R}\) Step 1: Find the normal reaction. The downward aerodynamic force adds to the weight of the car. \(N=mg+F_L\) Step 2: Find the magnitude of aerodynamic force. Since the car moves in a circle, friction provides the required centripetal force. At limiting friction,\(f=\mu_sN\) Also,\(f=\dfrac{mv^2}{R}\) Therefore, \(\mu_sN=\frac{mv^2}{R} \quad [\because N=mg+F_L] \\ \Rightarrow \mu_s(mg+F_L)=\frac{mv^2}{R} \\ \Rightarrow mg+F_L=\frac{mv^2}{\mu_sR} \\ \Rightarrow F_L=\frac{mv^2}{\mu_sR}-mg \\ \Rightarrow F_L=m\left(\frac{v^2}{\mu_sR}-g\right)\) Hence, option(1)is the correct answer.

If the radius of the curved road is changed to \(48\) m and the coefficient of friction between the tyres and the road remains the same, then the maximum allowed speed would be:
1. \(12\) m/s
2. \(24\) m/s
3. \(32\) m/s
4. \(44\) m/s
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(v=\sqrt{\mu rg}\) Step: Find the new maximum allowed speed. The maximum allowed speed of the particle is given by; \(v=\sqrt{\mu rg}\) \(\Rightarrow v \propto \sqrt{r}\) The ratio of allowed speed is given by; \(\Rightarrow \frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}} =\sqrt{\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}}\) \(\Rightarrow v_{2} =v_{1}\times \sqrt{\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}}= 30\times \sqrt{\frac{48}{75}}\) \(\Rightarrow v_2 = 30\times \sqrt{\frac{16}{25}}= 30\times\frac{4}{5}= 24~\text{m/s}\) Hence, option (2) is the correct answer.

In the arrangement shown in figure \(a_1,a_2,a_3\text{ and } a_4\) are the accelerations of masses \(m_1,m_2,m_3\text{ and }m_4\) respectively. Which of the following relation is true for this arrangement?

1. \(4 a_1+2 a_2+a_3+a_4=0 \)
2. \(a_1+4 a_2+3 a_3+a_4=0 \)
3. \( \mathrm{a}_1+4 \mathrm{a}_2+3 \mathrm{a}_3+2 \mathrm{a}_4=0 \)
4. \( 2 a_1+2 a_2+3 a_3+a_4=0\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(\Sigma \vec{T}.\vec{a}=0\) Step: Find the correct relation among the acceleration. The main concept is each movable pulley doubles the effect of the string constraint below it. First consider the bottom pully with mass\((m_3, m_4)\). For a movable pulley; \(a_3 +a_4 = 2a_{p_{3}}~~~...(1)\) (where \(a_{p_{3}}\)​ = acceleration of \(3^\text{rd}\) pulley) Now consider middle pully with mass\(m_2\) Now this pulley is also movable, and its motion is tied to the bottom pulley: \(a_2 + a_{p_{3}} = 2a_{p_{2}}~~~...(2)\) Now consider top pully with mass\(m_1\); \(a_1 + a_{p_{2}}=0\) \(\Rightarrow a_1 =- a_{p_{2}}~~~...(3)\) From equation\((2)~\text{and}~(3) \)we get; \(a_2 + a_{p_{3}} = -2a_1\) \(\Rightarrow a_{p_{3}} = -2a_1-a_2 ~~~...(4)\) From equation\((1)~\text{and}~(4) \)we get; \(a_3+a_4 = 2(-2a_1-a_2)\) \(\Rightarrow 4a_1+2a_2+a_3+a_4 =0\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

A smooth wire of length \(2\pi r\) is bent into a circle and kept in a vertical plane. A bead can slide smoothly on the wire. When the circle is rotating with angular speed \(\omega\) about the vertical diameter \(AB,\) as shown in figure, the bead is at rest with respect to the circular ring at position \(P\) as shown. Then the value of \(\omega^2\) is equal to:


1. \(\dfrac{g\sqrt{3}}{r}\)
2. \(\dfrac{2g}{r}\)
3. \(\dfrac{g\sqrt{3}}{2r}\)
4. \(\dfrac{2g}{\sqrt{3}r}\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:Balance forces along tangential and normal direction. Step 1:Draw the diagram. Step 2:Find the value of\(\tan\theta.\) \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{r/2}{r'}\) \(\Rightarrow\tan\theta=\dfrac{r/2}{\sqrt{r^2-r^2/4}}\) \(\Rightarrow \tan\theta=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\) Step 3:Findthe value of\(\omega^2.\) \(mg\sin \theta=m\omega^2\dfrac{r}{2}\cos\theta\) \(\Rightarrow 2g\tan \theta=\omega^2r\) \(\Rightarrow \omega^2=\dfrac{2 g \tan\theta}{r}\) \(\Rightarrow \omega^2=\dfrac{2 g }{\sqrt3 r}\) Hence, option (4)is the correct answer.
